question: Is topology-preserving dual nominal/certified construction with level-local child-bound finalization a distinct mechanism or known construction-bound reuse?
scope: A metric-tree bulk construction: M-tree, Slim-tree, PM-tree, VP/MVP, GNAT
B integrated bounds in GPU BVH, kd/R spatial hierarchies
C actual same computed distance used for construction decisions and pruning metadata, versus a separate bound/refit traversal
D directed-rounding conservative numerical controls; distinguish generic arithmetic from index construction

criteria.kill_generic: Same metric build distances directly derive query bounds with no independent object-distance certification pass. CPU qualifies.
criteria.kill_gpu_only: Moving that generic recipe to GPU or parallel reduction alone is not algorithm novelty.
criteria.high_system_risk: Topology build plus bound finalization is standard in spatial hierarchies; distinguish stage integration from literal single-kernel fusion.
criteria.pass: All dependency, numeric dual-path preservation and physical level-local ownership/lifetime differences established against nearest sources; absence in this finite search is not global novelty proof.
criteria.conditional: Generic recipe is known, but the joint native-topology/directly-rounded certificate/level-local producer contract is not established in checked nearest sources; only design a cheap differentiation test, not implement now.
criteria.kill_full: Nearest source demonstrably covers the joint claimed mechanism, not merely one control component.

search_policy: Primary papers, author/institution-hosted copies and exact-version official source. Search snippets and negative searches are leads, not evidence. Unsupported refit-removal/rounding claims remain UNKNOWN.
